title: FPGA Stereo Visual SLAM with Efficient Stereo Feature Matching and Key-frame Generation
conference: 2025 35th International Conference on Field-Programmable Logic and Applications (FPL)
summary: Helps a robot use two cameras to track its movement and build a map. Custom FPGA hardware matches image features faster, while selective map updates help keep tracking stable.

title: Hardware-Efficient Homogenized Key-Point Selection for Visual SLAM
conference: 2024 International Conference on Field Programmable Technology (ICFPT)
summary: Selects useful visual landmarks evenly across an image so a robot can track its movement reliably. The FPGA design handles this task efficiently as the number of image features changes.
image_alt: Concept diagram: many detected landmarks in a camera view are reduced to a more evenly distributed subset of the same landmarks.
image_label: Enlarge the keypoint selection concept diagram

title: Hardware Accelerator for Feature Matching with Binary Search Tree
conference: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS)
summary: Matches visual landmarks between images to help a robot track its movement. An organized search on FPGA makes matching about 12 times faster than checking every possible match on FPGA.
image_alt: Concept diagram: five corresponding landmarks are linked across two camera views to illustrate visual feature matching.
image_label: Enlarge the feature matching concept diagram

title: Dynamically Growing Neural Network Architecture for Lifelong Deep Learning on the Edge
conference: 2020 30th International Conference on Field-Programmable Logic and Applications (FPL)
summary: Supports neural networks that learn new tasks over time on small, resource-limited devices. The FPGA design reuses computing resources to make this ongoing learning more efficient.
image_alt: Concept diagram: a self-organizing neural network grows new neurons and connections as new objects are learned, within an FPGA accelerator.
image_label: Enlarge the SONN accelerator concept diagram

title: Feasibility Study of a Novel Cross Assembled Multi-quadrotor UAV
conference: 2018 IEEE International Conference on Information and Automation for Sustainability (ICIAfS)
summary: Contributed to building and testing a drone assembled from multiple quadrotor units. The study explored stable flight, reuse of existing flight controls, and replaceable modules.
image_alt: Concept diagram: four quadrotor modules, each with four rotors, are joined in a cross-shaped airframe and controlled by one shared controller.
